evidence.description: Spec 083 FR-001; the registration surface exists only as invite redemption and the one-time first-run setup. Exercised by the Phase 2 acceptance script against staging: direct registration attempts (form posts without a code, code-shaped guesses) must all fail.

falsification_tests: Any account existing in the cloud identity store whose creation record is neither an invite redemption nor the first-run glassbreak setup; or a scripted registration attempt without a valid invite code that results in a created account or a usable session.
claims.text: No account can be created in the cloud edition except by redeeming a valid invite code or through the one-time first-run setup that creates the glassbreak admin. There is no open registration path.

evidence.description: Spec 083 FR-002; codes are CSPRNG-generated (>=128 bits), stored only as hashes in D1, carry an expiry (default 7 days), a single-use redemption flag, and a revocation flag; redemption is an atomic check-and-consume.

falsification_tests: Redeeming the same code twice (two accounts or two sessions from one code), redeeming a code after its expiry, or redeeming a revoked code, in any case succeeds.
A plaintext invite code found in the identity database, in any log, or in any repository file.
claims.text: Invite codes are single-use, expiring (default 7 days from creation), and revocable by an admin at any time before redemption; codes are stored only as hashes, and a code that is used, expired, or revoked can never create an account.

evidence.description: Spec 083 FR-003 + User Story 1; the deploy pipeline issues a one-time setup code (CSPRNG, single-use, 24-hour expiry) shown once to the deploying operator's terminal; the owner sets the glassbreak password himself on the setup screen; the setup route disables permanently once an admin exists.

Amendment 3 (owner, 2026-10-30): the glassbreak seed record carries the account email tristen.pierson@gmail.com as its contact identifier, and at go-live the one-time setup code plus the production URL are delivered to the owner as the glassbreak account prompt; the password is set by the owner on the setup screen and is never collected by the agent.

falsification_tests: The setup route accepting a code, or serving its form, after the glassbreak admin exists; or a second admin being creatable through the setup path.

The glassbreak password, or any reversible form of it, found in chat records, repository files, deployment logs, or pipeline artifacts (the salted password hash in the identity database is the only permitted residue).
claims.text: The glassbreak admin is seeded exactly once, through a first-run setup gated by a single-use setup code that expires within 24 hours; the owner chooses the password himself on the setup screen, and no password or password-equivalent ever passes through chat, code, configuration, or logs. After setup completes, the setup path is permanently closed.

evidence.description: Spec 083 FR-004; sessions are opaque CSPRNG tokens (>=256 bits) stored hashed in D1, carried in an HttpOnly + Secure + SameSite cookie; the only unauthenticated surfaces are the login, invite, setup, robots, and static shell-asset routes; logout and admin disable delete the session rows.

Amendment 2 (owner, 2026-10-30): with staging cancelled, the login wall is the deployment's stated protection, so FR-004 enumerates the anonymous surface and the falsifier enumerates the anonymous-access test, including a payload scan of anonymously fetched shell/assets against the dataset.

falsification_tests: Any data-bearing cloud route returning content to a request with no session, a forged session value, or an expired session.
A session belonging to a disabled or removed user continuing to authenticate after the disable/removal is recorded.
A session token readable from page JavaScript (cookie missing HttpOnly) or found unhashed in the identity database.

An anonymous request to any route outside the enumerated public surface (login, setup while open, invite acceptance, robots.txt, static shell assets) returning anything other than a redirect-to-login or a 401.

An anonymous fetch of the SPA shell or its assets whose payload contains project data - a dataset record, a workspace or program name drawn from the dataset, or a project count - as found by scanning anonymously fetched payloads against the served dataset.
claims.text: Every cloud-edition surface except login, invite redemption, the first-run setup (while open), robots.txt, and the static shell assets requires a valid user session; sessions are opaque, hashed at rest, cookie-carried with HttpOnly/Secure/SameSite, and are revoked immediately on logout, disable, or removal. The login wall is the deployment's protection (Amendment 2): for anonymous requests every other route returns a redirect-to-login or 401, and no project data - records, names, counts, or content-bearing payloads - is served anonymously in any form; the dataset hydrates only after authentication.

evidence.description: Spec 083 FR-015..FR-017 + Amendment 1's adopted access matrix (the conventional GitHub/Slack/Notion two-axis pattern): enforcement at the edge Worker for global/admin surfaces and at the container API for workspace scope, following Spec 081's scoped-404 pattern. The terminal is a global Admin/Owner facility in the cloud edition (D-5).

falsification_tests: A member session receiving anything other than 403 from any admin API, or anything other than a scoped 404 (with no workspace data) for a workspace the member holds no role in.
A member session successfully invoking the terminal, user management, invite management, workspace management, or the publish action.
A Guest-type account holding, or being granted through any API, a per-workspace role above Viewer.
claims.text: Access is enforced on two axes on every request (Amendment 1): global user types (Owner - singular, the glassbreak account; Admin; Member; Guest, capped at Viewer) crossed with per-workspace roles (Owner/Admin/Member/Viewer/none), held independently per workspace. Admins manage users, invites, memberships, workspaces, and the terminal; members work only inside workspaces they hold a role in, see scoped 404s for workspaces they do not belong to, and cannot reach admin surfaces, other members' account data, or the terminal.

evidence.description: Spec 083 FR-006 + the publish pipeline design; the bundle builder works from an allowlist of sources (publishable tables, publishable checkout paths) and a structural exclusion of restricted stores (raw scans, page previews, restricted folders), then a marker scan over every artifact against the maintained restricted-marker list. Custody rule it mechanizes: statistics publishable, scans never redistributed.

falsification_tests: Canary test: a file carrying a restricted marker planted in a publishable source reaches the produced bundle, or the publish completes instead of failing on the planted marker.
An independent scan of the deployed cloud dataset (database export + hydrated files) finding any restricted marker, any restricted-source filename, or any scan/preview image.
claims.text: The cloud dataset is built only from publishable state by the publish pipeline: sources are allowlisted, restricted stores are structurally excluded, and every artifact in the produced bundle passes a restricted-marker scan before upload. A failed scan fails the publish — no bundle is uploaded, and restricted material (the CISI class: scans and their derivatives) can never enter the cloud dataset.

evidence.description: Spec 083 FR-007; the edge Worker sets X-Robots-Tag: noindex, nofollow on every response it passes (app pages, API responses, errors, static assets), and the app serves a robots.txt that disallows all paths; the login wall is the third layer. Owner order 2026-10-30: robots kept away until he lifts it.

falsification_tests: The standing header-check script finding any sampled response from either hostname (staging or production) — including an API error response and a static asset — without the X-Robots-Tag: noindex header, or a robots.txt that permits any path.
claims.text: Neither cloud hostname is indexable: every response carries X-Robots-Tag: noindex, nofollow, robots.txt disallows everything, and all data surfaces sit behind the login wall. This holds until the owner lifts it by name.

evidence.description: Spec 083 FR-008; Spec 082's token continues to govern desktop installs and first-party automation only. In the cloud, browsers authenticate as users; the edge-to-Cloud-Run service credential is a per-deployment secret held only in platform secret stores and injected by the edge, never rendered into any page, response, or client-visible configuration.

falsification_tests: Presenting a desktop install token to the cloud edge (as cookie or Authorization header) yielding any authenticated access.
The edge-to-Cloud-Run service credential appearing in any client-visible response, page source, log line, or repository file.
claims.text: User sessions are the only browser credential in the cloud edition. The Spec 082 per-install token is never accepted by the cloud edge, and the edge-to-Cloud-Run service credential exists only in platform secret stores — never in a page, a response, or the repository.

evidence.description: Architecture route study SS1/SS3/SS4: the container runs the same glossa_lab code and the same applied-epistemic-engineering library at the pinned >=1.5.0 line through the same aee_core adapter. The regression set is the GAP-ENV 23-claim set, including the five sign_val claims whose expected evidence value is 0.1625 under AEE 1.5.x (16 claims at that value).

falsification_tests: Any claim in the pinned regression set scoring differently in the cloud edition than on the desktop at the same AEE version, or the cloud image resolving an AEE version outside the pinned >=1.5.0,<1.6 range.
claims.text: The cloud edition assesses claims with the same AEE library at the program's pinned version, through the same adapter code as the desktop app, so a claim's score means the same thing in both editions.

evidence.description: Spec 083 FR-010 as revised by Amendment 4; pipelines execute as Cloud Run Job executions of the cloud image (runner entrypoint: hydrate, drain, export, exit); job state is journaled to the bundle store (Google Cloud Storage) on cadence and at completion, with the SIGTERM handler flushing the journal inside the platform's 10-second shutdown grace; the stall watchdog runs as a scheduled pass (a job without heartbeat past the stall window is marked failed with the reason recorded), and hydration restores job state before any execution resumes work.

falsification_tests: Killing a job's Cloud Run execution mid-run, or recycling the service instance mid-job, leaves the job in a non-terminal 'running' state past the stall window, or the job's record vanishes from the dataset.
claims.text: A job started in the cloud edition reaches a terminal state — completed, or failed with the reason recorded — across service scale-to-zero, instance recycling, and redeploy boundaries. Jobs execute as Cloud Run Job executions of the cloud image; they are never silently lost and never hang in a false 'running' state. (Revised by Amendment 4: the execution venue changed, the guarantee did not.)

evidence.description: Spec 083 FR-011; the session identity is propagated from the edge into the container API and stamped on created/modified records (claims, digestion acts, study actions, anchor edits); surfaces render the actor's username. Digestion is by named humans (Spec 029 lane 2), so attribution is a correctness property, not decoration.

falsification_tests: Any claim, digestion act, or study action performed by a signed-in test member whose stored record lacks that member's user id, or whose surface rendering omits the actor.
claims.text: Every act performed in the cloud edition — registering or explaining a claim, a digestion act, running a study or job, editing anchors or data — is recorded with the acting user's identity and displays that attribution on the relevant surfaces.

evidence.description: Spec 083 FR-012; the audit log is a D1 table written by the edge for identity events and by the container for publishes, append-only through the application (no update/delete path exists in the admin API), and viewable in the admin dashboard.

falsification_tests: Performing any listed action (login success or failure, invite create/redeem/revoke, role change, disable, removal, setup completion, dataset publish) and finding no corresponding audit entry with actor and timestamp.
An audit entry being modified or deleted through any application surface.
claims.text: Security-relevant events — logins (success and failure), invite creation/redemption/revocation, role changes, account disable/removal, the first-run setup, and dataset publishes — are written to an append-only audit log with actor and timestamp, readable in the admin dashboard and not editable through any application surface.

evidence.description: Spec 083 FR-013 + publish pipeline design; a bundle is a manifest (bundle id, build time, source commit, per-artifact SHA-256) plus artifacts in Google Cloud Storage; hydration verifies every artifact against the manifest and swaps the working dataset only when the whole bundle verifies; the Status surface shows the served bundle id and source commit.

falsification_tests: Interrupting a hydration mid-way leaving the served dataset mixed (sampled artifacts matching neither the old nor the new manifest in full).
The Status surface showing a bundle id or source commit that does not match the manifest of the dataset actually served.
claims.text: The cloud dataset is versioned and honestly labelled: every publish produces a manifest (bundle id, build time, source commit, per-artifact hashes); hydration is atomic — the served dataset is always exactly one manifest, never a mixture — and the Status surface displays the bundle actually being served.

evidence.description: Amendment 2 (owner, 2026-10-30): staging is cancelled - the login wall is the protection - so verification runs against local production-shaped builds and ephemeral preview deployments, the proof battery runs before the production deploy, and go-live follows the proofs directly.

falsification_tests: A staging hostname resolving, or staging resources on either platform (Cloudflare: a staging project, database, or bucket; Google: a second Cloud Run service, job, or storage bucket) existing for this edition at any time.
Production serving traffic before the pre-launch proof record (claim-test results, canary/scan gate results, the adversarial pass, and the noindex checks) exists in the rollout record.
claims.text: Rollout is production-only (Amendment 2; decision D-7 cancelled): exactly one deployment exists, at glossa.bitconcepts.tech, and no staging hostname or staging resources are ever created. The full flow is proven against a production-shaped local build and ephemeral preview deployments, and the pre-launch proof battery - claim-test suites, the planted-canary and marker-scan gates, a fresh adversarial pass over the auth surface, and the noindex header checks - passes before the production deploy; go-live follows the proofs directly and is recorded in the rollout record.

evidence.description: Spec 083 FR-015 + Amendment 1 SS1: the publish pipeline assigns all existing project state to the seeded primary workspace, with the publish report reconciling counts per resource class against the source.

falsification_tests: Any resource in the served cloud dataset lacking a workspace assignment, or assigned in the first bundle to any workspace other than the primary workspace.
The seeding publish report's count for any resource class differing from the source dataset's count for that class.
claims.text: At the cloud edition's first publish, a primary workspace named 'Indus Script' is seeded and receives all existing project state: every project resource in the published dataset is assigned to that workspace, the publish report's per-class counts reconcile exactly with the source dataset, and no resource is ever served unscoped.

evidence.description: Spec 083 FR-016 + Amendment 1 SS1/SS4 (decision D-1 applied: workspace creation is an admin act); the admin Workspaces tab is wireframe 09.

falsification_tests: A Member- or Guest-type account creating or archiving a workspace through any route or API.
Any surface of an archived workspace returning content to a non-admin user.
claims.text: Only global Admin and Owner accounts can create or archive workspaces. An archived workspace serves nothing: every one of its surfaces answers scoped 404 to non-admin users.

evidence.description: Spec 083 FR-017 + Amendment 1 SS2's adopted matrix (per-workspace Owner/Admin/Member/Viewer), enforced at the edge and in the container API, which binds scoped queries to the identity's entitled workspace ids itself.

falsification_tests: A Viewer-role user mutating any content in that workspace, or a Member-role user changing workspace membership or settings, through any route.
A user exercising, in a second workspace, powers that derive only from a role they hold in a first workspace.
claims.text: A user's effective powers inside a workspace are exactly their per-workspace role, with global Admin/Owner holding implicit Workspace Admin: Viewers cannot mutate workspace content, Members cannot manage workspace membership or settings, and a role held in one workspace confers nothing in another.

evidence.description: Spec 083 FR-017 + Amendment 1 SS3: workspace scope is carried by every resource, queries and aggregates (search, lists, counts, badges, the switcher) are computed inside the viewer's memberships, closing the badge-scoping gap recorded in Spec 081's closeout.

falsification_tests: Any response to a user lacking a role in workspace W - including search results, list payloads, counts, and badges - containing any of W's resource identifiers, titles, or counts.
A direct request by such a user for any enumerated resource class of W returning anything other than a scoped 404 with no data.
claims.text: No cross-workspace leakage exists in any form: a user without a role in a workspace receives a scoped 404 for every resource class of that workspace (workspaces; claims and their records including digestion; evidence and sources; anchor sets and data surfaces; studies; experiments and analysis runs; jobs and results; discovery items; research-loop sessions; notebooks; reports; foundation status), and that workspace contributes nothing to their search results, lists, counts, or badges.

evidence.description: Spec 083 FR-017 + Amendment 1 SS4: the per-user workspace-access matrix (wireframe 10) reads and writes the same grant store the enforcement path reads, and role changes revoke sessions immediately (FR-004), so an edit is effective on the next request.

falsification_tests: The access view showing a workspace grant that does not exist in the identity store, or omitting one that does.
An access edit (grant, role change, or revocation) made in the dashboard not being reflected in the target user's enforcement on their next request.
claims.text: The admin dashboard's per-user workspace-access view is accurate and effective: it displays exactly the grants stored for that user (no phantom grants, none missing), and an edit made through it is the enforcement reality on the target user's next request.
